key_insight: The paper introduces a scalable ML interatomic potential that cleanly separates long-range electrostatics from local learned interactions, enabling efficient prediction of energies, forces, stresses, and electrical response at million-atom scale.
engineering_relevance: This advances atomistic modeling for device-relevant materials under electric fields by making long-range physics compatible with distributed, GPU-parallel simulation.
method: Analytically split electrostatic forces and Born effective charges into a global electrostatics solve plus local derivatives of learned latent charges.
Embed the formulation in an equivariant MLIP backbone (DPA4C-LR) to preserve spatial decomposability for distributed evaluation.
Support energies, forces, stresses, and BECs across boundary conditions while retaining scalability on the nvalchemi platform.
evidence_signal: The model scales to 5.2 million atoms on four GPUs at about twice the cost of the short-range backbone and reproduces field-dependent IR spectra, polarization hysteresis, ionic conductivity, and interface thermal transport benchmarks.
watch_item: The approach still relies on correct electrostatics setup and slab/boundary-condition handling, so implementation details may strongly affect accuracy and scalability.
paper_title: Scalable long-range machine learning interatomic potentials with electrical response for atomistic material modeling
